title: Empirical Evaluation of a Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Pipeline: A Paired Study with gpt-5‑mini on 400 Intent→Configuration Tasks
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (CAND‑2026‑002) to measure operational failure rates of LLM‑generated network configuration changes and the effect of a lightweight automated validator (with at most one deterministic LLM repair call). Using gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted NetOps adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) on 400 unique public/synthetic intent tasks (paired Baseline=Direct‑apply vs Guarded=validator+≤1 repair) in sandboxed emulator replicas, we observed zero operational failures in both arms (n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The paired difference (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI 0.00–0.00, 10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.0. Critically, the experiment used a shared initial candidate generation semantics (independent_condition_generation=false), so the Guarded condition could only differ from Baseline when the validator rejected the shared candidate and a repair call produced a different validated candidate. In this run the validator issued 0 rejects and 0 repair calls; therefore the two conditions were identical for every task. We release the full preregistration, execution manifest, scoring artifacts, and analysis scripts. We discuss operational implications, explain why the null outcome is informative yet limited, and catalogue threats to validity and next steps.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed for intent‑driven NetOps tasks (intent→configuration, remediation, limited self‑healing). Operational deployment requires evidence about realistic failure rates and about the marginal benefit of lightweight automated validators and bounded repair loops. We preregistered study CAND‑2026‑002 to answer: What are realistic failure rates of LLM‑generated configuration changes in sandboxed heterogeneous networks, and how much does a deterministic validator (with at most one LLM repair call) reduce those failures? Contributions: (1) a machine‑readable preregistration and full archived execution manifest; (2) a paired confirmatory run (400 unique intents, two conditions) using gpt‑5‑mini and a hosted adapter; (3) transparent reporting of results (zero observed failures) and a frank analysis of design choices (notably the shared‑candidate generation semantics) that shape interpretability.
sections.related_work: We situate this study among recent work on LLMs for NetOps, generate–validate–repair loops, and verifier‑guided IaC repair. Representative references used in design and motivation include: a comprehensive survey of LLM‑based network management and evaluation recommendations [W4415071524], intent→configuration studies and small LLM deployment reports (doi:10.1002/nem.2313), RAG/validator literature and factuality studies [W4401857375], verifier‑guided IaC repair architectures (TerraFormer, W7124141852), and applied LLM for IaC/self‑healing proposals (W7124141852; doi:10.2139/ssrn.6608518). We relied on these verified sources to motivate paired, validator‑aware experimental designs rather than simple model leaderboards.
sections.methodology: Preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002) — design frozen before execution. Key elements: adapter_family=hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model=gpt‑5‑mini; paired binary design with conditions Baseline (Direct‑apply) and Guarded (validator + at most one deterministic LLM repair); task_count=400 unique intents; completed_episode_count=800. Generation semantics and condition coupling — preregistration set independent_condition_generation=false and generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate": a single initial candidate configuration was generated per intent and shared across conditions. Guarded differed from Baseline only if the deterministic validator rejected that shared candidate and the pipeline invoked (and accepted) a single deterministic LLM repair call to produce a different validated candidate. Rationale for shared_initial design — reduces variance from generation sampling and isolates the validator+repair as the only active intervention. Execution and logging — preserved prompts, model outputs, adapter traces, scoring JSON, and SHA‑256 artifact hashes (see execution_manifest). Scoring and operational failure definition — automated emulator checks for reachability/policy violations and application errors recorded in per‑task scoring JSON (archived). Analysis plan — preregistered primary estimand: paired difference in operational failure proportion (P(failure|Direct‑apply) − P(failure|Guarded)); analysis used McNemar exact test and bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI with 10k resamples (seed=1729). All scripts, seeds, and hashes are archived.
sections.results: Execution summary — run started 2026‑08‑24T21:08:22Z and completed 2026‑08‑24T21:56:41Z; completed_episode_count=800; model_calls_used=400; no infrastructure failures recorded. Primary confirmatory outcome — every paired intent succeeded operationally in both conditions: n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; baseline_success_rate=1.0, guarded_success_rate=1.0. Primary statistics: paired difference (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.00; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.0. Validator/repair activity (required revision #1) — the archived execution and analysis artifacts show: validator_reject_count = 0; deterministic_repair_calls_invoked = 0; final_applied_candidate differed from the shared initial candidate in 0/400 tasks. Representative preserved response artifacts (identical Baseline/Guarded shared candidate hashes) — examples (filename : SHA‑256): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt : f8de4d6e1a625e42ba4907440b4377c78949ed56446e5c73030bc267e56abfaf; execution/responses/task-000100-shared-initial.txt : 6875822669e63d330158f227ed639c628326b64dc735498d397585c059302c9c; execution/responses/task-000400-shared-initial.txt : bf23fccddc1ec709d3d5089eb80a82c229bece6f475f5c120cb7a935abaf296d. Deterministic reconciliation — provider_call_audit shows stage_counts:{"shared_initial_generation":400} and condition_counts:{"shared":400}, confirming the shared‑candidate design and that no per‑condition generation occurred.
sections.discussion: Why a null result? The run produced a degenerate paired contingency (all n11). That outcome is an informative boundary case but is not evidence that validators are unnecessary in general. Interpretations supported by archived artifacts: (A) task scope and distribution — the 400 selected intents (public/synthetic, modest scope) appear to fall within the model+adapter competence envelope for the shared generation semantics; (B) shared_initial design — because independent_condition_generation=false, Guarded could only have altered outcomes if the deterministic validator had rejected the shared candidate and repair produced an accepted alternative; no such events occurred; (C) emulator/validator sensitivity — we did not run injected positive controls to empirically demonstrate the scorer's sensitivity to simulated failures (limitation below), so a residual risk exists that the scoring pipeline could miss some classes of failure. Implications — in narrowly scoped, benign intent classes and under the shared‑candidate design, the studied LLM+adapter produced no observable operational failures in the emulator; this cannot be extrapolated to broader, adversarial, or production settings. Required reviewer clarifications addressed: we now report validator_reject_count=0 and repair_calls_invoked=0 and we explicitly justify and document the preregistered shared_initial generation choice and its interpretational consequences. Future work — (i) independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation=true) to enable sample‑level divergence between Baseline and Guarded, (ii) adversarial/harder intents and injected failing controls to exercise validator/recovery behavior, and (iii) multi‑model and vendor diversity experiments.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment testing a validator+single‑repair intervention versus direct application on 400 intent→configuration tasks using gpt‑5‑mini and a hosted NetOps adapter. Observed outcome: zero operational failures in both arms. Because the design used a shared initial candidate per intent and the validator recorded 0 rejects, Guarded never applied a repaired alternative; thus the experimental contrast was inert in this run. The result documents a reproducible boundary case (low‑difficulty, shared candidate) rather than a general safety guarantee. We publish full artifacts and hashes to enable follow‑ups that vary generation semantics, introduce adversarial inputs, and include positive controls for scorer sensitivity.

Prompting strategy and generation semantics: preregistered with independent_condition_generation=false and generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate" (i.e., one shared initial candidate per intent, both conditions start from the same generated candidate). Permitted tools and capabilities: hosted model API (OpenAI hosted for gpt‑5‑mini), sandboxed emulator replicas assembled from public topology examples, and a deterministic validator implementing generate_validate_repair_v1 limited to one LLM repair call per failing validation. Preregistration/freeze: preregistration CAND‑2026‑002 was completed and frozen prior to any model calls (documented in artifacts). Autonomous literature verification, experiment execution, and analysis were performed by the autonomous researcher; artifacts and verification records are archived. The Research Director retained oversight only for pre‑lock choices; all research question selection, preregistration finalization, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript drafting were autonomous after the lock. Full archived artifacts, hashes, and analysis scripts are available in the execution_manifest referenced by this submission.
limitations: Single‑model and single‑adapter run (gpt‑5‑mini with hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Results do not generalize across models, adapters, or orchestration stacks.

Shared initial candidate generation (independent_condition_generation=false) means Baseline and Guarded begin from the same generated candidate; Guarded can only differ if the validator rejects and a repair produces an accepted alternative. In this run validator_reject_count=0 and repair_calls_invoked=0, so the experimental contrast was inert.
Task set scope: 400 intents were assembled from public/synthetic sources and may underrepresent production complexity and adversarial inputs.

Emulator and validator fidelity: no injected positive controls (synthetic failing tasks) were run to empirically demonstrate the scorer/validator sensitivity; therefore potential scorer false negatives cannot be empirically excluded in this dataset.

Operational realism: no live production devices, canary staging, human operator interventions, or multi‑vendor hardware idiosyncrasies were included; external validity for production deployments is limited.

Because all paired outcomes were successes, statistical inference about validator efficacy for harder tasks is limited — absence of observed failures prevents quantifying potential reductions in high‑impact failure rates.
